prompt:
You are a senior information designer and editorial typographer who sets data tables for high-quality publications (statistical yearbooks, reference works, financial reports, technical documentation) in many writing systems, including Chinese. You judge by looking at the real rendered result.

Judge a table layout on all of these levels, in this order of necessity but as one whole:
1. correctness — every character visible, structure intact, nothing clipped or overlapping;
2. readability — natural line breaks, words/numbers/identifiers/semantic units kept whole, continuous reading;
3. function — easy to look up, compare, locate and understand the information for this table's real reading tasks;
4. visual order — alignment, grouping, hierarchy, consistent scale for elements with the same role;
5. visual rhythm — proportion, density changes, distribution of white space, spatial relationships;
6. overall aesthetics — balance, restraint, naturalness, harmony.
Do not assume that equal widths, symmetry, minimum height, the fewest lines, the golden ratio or any fixed proportion is good in itself; decide from this table's function, content and reading task, and look for counter-examples to your own rules.

Table: [val] Extreme · 10 columns + unbreakable values (language en).
Grid: 10 columns × 4 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Measured content facts (text px at 15px font, padding excluded):
  col 1: header "ID" · longest unbreakable unit 16px · widest one-line content 16px
  col 2: header "SKU" · longest unbreakable unit 44px · widest one-line content 136px
  col 3: header "Color" · longest unbreakable unit 40px · widest one-line content 40px
  col 4: header "Size" · longest unbreakable unit 31px · widest one-line content 31px
  col 5: header "Qty" · longest unbreakable unit 26px · widest one-line content 26px
  col 6: header "Price" · longest unbreakable unit 41px · widest one-line content 41px
  col 7: header "Tax" · longest unbreakable unit 32px · widest one-line content 32px
  col 8: header "Total" · longest unbreakable unit 47px · widest one-line content 47px
  col 9: header "Warehouse" · longest unbreakable unit 81px · widest one-line content 122px
  col 10: header "Tracking" · longest unbreakable unit 159px · widest one-line content 159px
Each column adds 21px of padding+border to its text width.
Viewport: 720px wide (dashed pink box in the renders). At 720px some words cannot fit unsplit. Horizontal scrolling is ALLOWED: the table may be wider than 720px (column widths summing to more than 719px) (the reader scrolls), or you may fit within 719px and accept the consequences. Fitting and scrolling layouts are judged as two separate classes; propose good layouts of BOTH kinds.
Rendering convention: a full render shows the WHOLE table; anything right of the dashed box is not clipped — it is reached by scrolling. Where a layout scrolls, an extra "viewport view" image shows only what is visible at first sight.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. Only the column widths are designed; row heights follow from them.

You are continuing your synthesis. Shown after the overview: s2A, s2B (full view, then viewport view), Layout R, s0B (full view, then viewport view), Layout S (full view, then viewport view).
Measured facts:
s2A: column widths [38, 55, 61, 52, 47, 62, 53, 68, 102, 180] px · table 719×448 px · row heights [36, 129, 153, 129] · column headers on >1 line: 0/10 · tallest cell 6 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 2 · fits the 720 px viewport (no scrolling)
s2B: column widths [38, 115, 61, 52, 47, 62, 53, 68, 102, 180] px · table 779×216 px · row heights [36, 60, 60, 60] · column headers on >1 line: 0/10 · tallest cell 2 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 0 · WIDER than the viewport by 59 px (horizontal scrolling)
Layout R: column widths [38, 95, 61, 52, 47, 62, 53, 68, 102, 140] px · table 719×216 px · row heights [36, 60, 60, 60] · column headers on >1 line: 0/10 · tallest cell 2 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 2 · fits the 720 px viewport (no scrolling)
s0B: column widths [38, 136, 61, 52, 47, 62, 53, 68, 102, 180] px · table 800×216 px · row heights [36, 60, 60, 60] · column headers on >1 line: 0/10 · tallest cell 2 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 0 · WIDER than the viewport by 80 px (horizontal scrolling)
Layout S: column widths [38, 157, 61, 52, 47, 62, 53, 68, 143, 180] px · table 862×146 px · row heights [36, 36, 36, 36] · column headers on >1 line: 0/10 · tallest cell 1 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 0 · WIDER than the viewport by 142 px (horizontal scrolling)

Look again at the renders. Critique each, then propose up to 3 further refinements, or set "done": true if further changes would not bring a meaningful improvement.
